newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens stock exchange ended up. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Athens stock exchange ended up. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline to delete reference to the exchange being "expected bearish")
Greek shares ended above 1,000 points on Wednesday for the first time in three weeks and market analysts predicted a sustained rally.
Nikos Katsomalos, managing director at Avax Securities, described 1996 as a bad year for the Athens bourse and said that the stock exchange's positive reactions were long overdue.

"Inflation had fallen to around 10 percent in May of 1995 and has taken a declining course over the past two years. Also, currently interest rates are dropping and these are positive economic signs that directly influence Greek stocks," Katsomalos said.

Meanwhile, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) rated Greece's stock exchange low, 22nd out of 30 emerging markets, but said the bourse had the lowest price earnings ratio (P/E of x10.17) and the highest dividend yield (of 6.28 percent) in the group which included Russia, Venezuela, China and others.

"Foreign investors have helped create an optimistic sentiment over Greek equities, along with institutional investors and a few individuals who have entered the Athens stock exchange," said Katsomalos.

He expected the majority of Greek individual investors to return to the Athens bourse after being convinced that growth funds will perform better than income funds after a long time that this has not happened.
The general share index closed up 1.24 percent or 12.32 points at 1002.30 from Tuesday's 989.98. It opened at 993.32. Trading volume rose to 8.4 billion drachmas on volume of 3.8 million share.
Gainers led losers 112 to 94 with 30 issues unchanged on 236 traded.
